overview: The Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee held its first community forum to present the feasibility study progress, technical findings, and project timeline for renovating or rebuilding the high school. The committee outlined an educational vision for a 1,395-student facility and shared data on current building deficiencies while establishing channels for public input.

items.title: Introductions and Project Background
items.summary: Chair Jenny Graham introduced the project team and reviewed the history of Medford's 2023 invitation into the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) core program.

items.title: Project Management and Design Teams
items.summary: Representatives from Leftfield, the owner’s project manager, and SMMA, the project architect, introduced their technical teams and respective roles in the feasibility phase.

items.title: Eligibility Phase and Enrollment Projections
items.summary: The committee finalized an enrollment target of 1,395 students for grades 9-12 and reached agreements to centralize pre-K services and the Medford Family Network within the project scope.

items.title: Project Schedule and Feasibility Study Phases
items.summary: The team presented a timeline targeting a February 2027 town vote and a September 2030 school opening. The current feasibility phase will evaluate code upgrades, renovations, or a new build, with a preferred option selected by June 2026.

items.title: Educational Vision and Building Deficiencies
items.summary: Officials identified significant mechanical, structural, and accessibility failures in the existing 1970s building and proposed a plan focused on flexible learning, improved Career Technical Education (CTE), and universal design.

items.title: Site Investigations and Technical Findings
items.summary: Technical surveys revealed the high school lacks fire protection systems, has significant roof ponding, and faces topographical challenges with an 80-foot grade change. Soil borings, hazardous material surveys, and traffic studies are ongoing to inform design alternatives.

items.title: Community Engagement and Advisory Teams
items.summary: The committee established four specialized advisory teams covering sustainability, safety, design, and equity to incorporate students and community experts into the planning process.

items.title: Upcoming Milestones and Public Input
items.summary: The Preliminary Design Program will be submitted in February 2026, followed by a community input session on March 5 to review the initial set of design alternatives.

items.title: Public Q&A Session
items.summary: The project team confirmed the new building will include air conditioning and addressed the cost implications of a swimming pool, noting that pools are not reimbursable by the state and would require local funding or donors.
